headline: High: shared filesystem/git and broad shell/network access create default risks of prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors between Claude Code and Plandex.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Both agents can read and write the filesystem, and Claude Code also uses MCP while Plandex can apply staged changes. That creates a plausible default bridge where one agent can ingest the other’s files or outputs as trusted content. This is not proven to be a raw-instruction parser hijack, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF either agent reads the other agent’s generated files without provenance checks, injected instructions can be followed.
IF a shared project directory is used as an exchange channel, prompt content can cross between agents.
mitigations: Use separate working directories for each agent.
Disable auto-apply or auto-run modes during cross-agent work.
Add a manual review step before either agent consumes the other’s output.
Prefix exchanged files with a strict machine-readable schema and reject free-form instructions.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging or content-signing for inter-agent files.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Claude Code touches git credentials and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, while both agents read/write repo files and the cwd. Plandex also sends data to a model provider or server backend. In a shared workspace, sensitive code or secrets can flow from A into B’s context and then out to third-party services. The shared-workspace path is plausible by default.
conditions: IF secrets or credentials are present in the shared repo or environment, either agent may read them.
IF Plandex sends project contents to its cloud or model provider, those contents can leave the local workspace.
mitigations: Remove secrets from the shared directory before running either agent.
Use a redacted clone or throwaway repo for cross-agent tasks.
Restrict Plandex to a self-hosted backend if available.
Rotate any credentials exposed in the workspace.
requires-engineering: enforce secret-scanning and automatic redaction before outbound API calls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can execute shell commands, write files, and modify git state. Claude Code’s shared state is via filesystem and git, while Plandex also stages and applies changes in the project directory. Concurrent writes to the same repo can overwrite each other or corrupt git state, and no locking is documented here. This is a default dangerous overlap.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same git checkout, concurrent edits can conflict.
IF either agent auto-applies changes while the other is still planning, one can overwrite the other’s work.
mitigations: Run the agents in separate clones.
Serialize write access with a simple manual lock file.
Disable auto-apply on Plandex during shared work.
Review git diffs before each apply.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level file locking and merge arbitration.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Plandex is a planner with review-then-apply behavior, so Claude Code’s outputs can become Plandex inputs and then turn into applied edits. Claude Code can also generate shell commands and file changes that Plandex may treat as authoritative if copied over. Because the pair lacks a documented verification boundary, a mistaken output can cascade into real repository changes.
conditions: IF Claude Code’s generated patch or command text is pasted into Plandex, Plandex may apply it with limited independent verification.
IF Plandex auto-apply is enabled, downstream edits can occur from unverified upstream output.
mitigations: Require a human diff review before apply.
Keep Plandex auto-apply disabled.
Ask each agent to restate assumptions before acting on the other’s output.
Use small, isolated tasks instead of end-to-end handoffs.
requires-engineering: add structured handoff contracts with validation checks.

E_compliance.rationale: No explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented in the profiles. The main compliance-relevant difference is that Plandex may use a cloud or model-provider backend, while Claude Code is tied to Anthropic APIs and local files. Without a stated regulated data class, the pair shows only a limited compliance gap, so low is appropriate.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into the shared workspace and Plandex routes it to a cloud backend, policy obligations may be triggered.
IF the deployment requires local-only processing, either agent’s outbound API use would violate that requirement.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared workspace.
Use a self-hosted Plandex backend if policy requires locality.
Document retention and deletion expectations before use.
Review vendor terms for both tools before handling sensitive data.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing and data-loss controls.
